NYX-007 (L3, US-SJC): Described as a "strong contributor" involved in cache coherence modeling discussions. This is an L3 (junior/individual contributor) level, and the language "strong contributor" and "involved in discussions" suggests active participation but not singular ownership, technical authority, or irreplaceable scope. NYX-013 (L3, US-SJC): Described as a "strong analog designer" who has been "picking up more responsibility" on the PMIC team, including "some layout review." Again, L3 level, and phrases like "picking up more responsibility" and "some layout review" indicate growing scope but not yet established organization-wide criticality, unique expertise, or a role where their departure would create a significant gap (e.g., no mention of being the only person with a given specialization, leading a workstream, or holding institutional knowledge others depend on).

Both employees appear to be solid, developing contributors at a junior level (L3) without documented evidence of broad organizational impact, singular expertise, leadership scope, or irreplaceability that would distinguish them as critical retention risks beyond the compa-ratio gap itself. Per instructions, compa-ratio/gap size alone (0.76 and 0.77) is not sufficient justification -- criticality requires evidence of role scope and seniority that neither summary substantiates. If more detail emerges (e.g., NYX-007 being the sole owner of a core cache coherence model, or NYX-013 being the only qualified layout reviewer on PMIC), that would change this assessment.</reasoning>
